paper_citation: Ryan Gibson, stego-lsb 1.7.1 software implementation, GitHub commit 06a3c920420e62f2e8a0589cfd5bfb2e51be4ee8.

payload_contract.content: same preregistered progressive raw-secret bitplanes used by FINAL-5J-v1

distortion_contract.selection: clean-valid candidate with realized cover-stego PSNR closest to the declared target

attack_contract.implementation: shared FINAL-5J attack functions and frozen seeds

adaptations.description: A self-contained grayscale NumPy implementation is used instead of importing the reference package. The reference commit establishes LSB lineage, not author-equivalent execution.
The task plan supplies payload length and k, avoiding a file-size header and allowing the exact progressive secret payload to be compared.
k is selected from a frozen candidate set by closest realized PSNR, with bit-exact clean recovery required.

limitations: This is a canonical engineering baseline, not a claim of exact reproduction of a peer-reviewed paper.
No ECC or semantic Base/Detail layer exists; those fields are not_applicable.
Repository CI and target-server dry-run verification remain required before production execution.
